mainTopic: Testimony about a husband's death: conflicting witnesses, why a צרה cannot testify for her rival, and the argument of רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא about a rival or mother-in-law eating תרומה.
overview: The amud opens with the last line of a משנה: when witnesses contradict each other about whether a husband died, his wife may not remarry. The גמרא then looks back at the earlier case of two co-wives, where the one who says 'he did not die' may not remarry. It explains that the words 'he did not die' do not mean a silent צרה could rely on her rival. They rule out the idea that she is lying just to spite her rival. Next the גמרא asks why רבי מאיר does not also disagree in that earlier clause. רבי אלעזר says he does. רבי יוחנן says even רבי מאיר agrees there, but a line of the משנה is a difficulty for רבי יוחנן, and it stays unanswered. A new משנה teaches that a wife who says her husband died may remarry, but her צרה or her חמות may not. רבי טרפון lets that other woman keep eating תרומה, while רבי עקיבא forbids her both. The גמרא explains why both cases were needed, rules like רבי טרפון, and אביי supports this from a later משנה showing that a rival wife's words are ignored.

steps.title: משנה: one woman says he died, another says he did not
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with a case of conflicting witnesses: one woman says the husband died and another says he did not die. His wife may not remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one woman says 'He died' and another woman says 'He did not die,' this one may not marry.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the משנה. It gives a ruling when two women give opposite reports about a missing husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line finishes the משנה's case of conflicting witnesses: one says 'he died' and one says 'he did not die,' and the same applies to two women. 'This one' is the wife whose husband is in question, and the conflicting reports stop her from remarrying. The גמרא's first question, in Step 2, is about an earlier line of the משנה on the previous amud, where two co-wives disagree.

phrases.english: A woman says: 'He died,'
and a woman says: 'He did not die' —
this one may not marry.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the wife whose husband is missing. The two women are only witnesses, and their reports cancel each other out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשָּׁה אוֹמֶרֶת מֵת וְאִשָּׁה אוֹמֶרֶת לֹא מֵת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one woman testifies that the husband died and another testifies that he did not die, his wife may not remarry.

steps.title: If she had stayed silent, could she remarry?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from the משנה: she is forbidden only because she said 'he did not die.' That would mean a silent wife could remarry, which seems to clash with the rule that a צרה cannot testify for her rival.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason she cannot marry is that she said 'He did not die.' So if she had stayed silent, would she be allowed to marry? But a rival wife may not testify for her fellow wife!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier clause of the משנה, where one co-wife says he died and the other says he did not die, so the one who said 'he did not die' may not remarry. It reads a hidden implication into that wording and attacks it, because the implication goes against a known rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By stressing that this wife said 'he did not die,' the משנה seems to suggest that silence would have been fine, so she could rely on the other wife's 'he died.' But a צרה is not believed to testify that the husband died so her rival can remarry. So silence should not help either, and the inference seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A rival wife (another wife of the same husband)
A rival wife may not testify for her fellow wife

steps.confusionAlert: The inference does not come from anything the משנה says directly. It comes only from the extra words 'he did not die.' The גמרא is asking why those words are needed.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The reason is that she said 'He did not die,'
phrases.notes: This points back to an earlier line of the משנה about two co-wives: the one who said he died may marry, and the one who said he did not die may not.

phrases.english: so if she was silent — she may marry?
But a rival wife may not testify for her fellow!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאָמְרָה לֹא מֵת הָא אִישְׁתִּיקָא תִּנָּשֵׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the earlier co-wife clause of the משנה (one co-wife says he died, the other says he did not die, so the one who said he did not die may not remarry) and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied ruling that a silent צרה could remarry based on the other wife's testimony.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A צרה is not believed to testify for her rival. So the second wife cannot rely on the first wife's word even if she stays silent. The משנה's emphasis on 'he did not die' therefore seems unnecessary or misleading.

steps.title: The words 'he did not die' were needed to block a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the inference is wrong. The משנה said 'he did not die' to rule out the idea that she is secretly lying just to hurt her rival, which might have led us to let her remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to say 'He did not die.' You might have thought: the husband really did die. When she says 'He did not die,' she means to ruin her rival wife, and she is saying, 'Let me die with the Philistines.' So the משנה teaches us that she still may not marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה needed the words 'he did not die.' It shows they are not hinting that silence would help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have suspected that the second wife knows he died and lies only to block her rival from remarrying. On that view she would be harming herself too, but she accepts it to hurt her rival, like שמשון saying 'let me die with the Philistines.' The משנה teaches that we do not assume this; we take her at her word, and she may not remarry.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (the תנא) to say
It would enter your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)
'Let me die with the Philistines': harming oneself in order to harm an enemy

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'he did not die' does not mean a silent צרה may remarry. It is there to rule out the idea that she is lying to spite her rival.

phrases.english: 'He did not die' was necessary for it,
it would enter your mind to say:
this man really did die,
and that which she says 'He did not die' —
she intends to ruin her rival wife,
and she is saying 'Let her soul die with the Philistines,'
phrases.notes: שופטים 16:30. She'd hurt herself too, but she accepts that to hurt her rival.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא מֵת אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by giving a different reason for the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a needed teaching (איצטריך): the wording rules out a mistaken assumption instead of implying a leniency.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She might be lying to spite her rival, so we might ignore her claim and let her remarry.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not assume she is lying. Since she said he did not die, she may not remarry.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי מאיר disagree in the first clause too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the משנה's case of 'one says he died, one says he was killed,' where רבי מאיר forbids remarriage because the reports conflict. It asks why רבי מאיר does not also disagree in the earlier 'died vs. did not die' clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One says he died, etc.' But then let רבי מאיר disagree in the first clause as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a later part of the משנה and asks why רבי מאיר's view is missing from an earlier part. This opens a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that conflicting reports, like 'died' versus 'killed,' block remarriage for both wives. 'Died' versus 'did not die' is an even stronger conflict. So he should have objected there too, and should forbid even the wife who said 'he died.'

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause (earlier part of the משנה)
Etc.: the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: 'One says: He died,' etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: and one says he was killed; רבי מאיר says that since they contradict each other, they may not marry.

phrases.english: But let Rabbi Meir disagree in the first clause!
phrases.notes: The first clause is the case where one wife says he died and the other says he did not die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about a different clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that רבי מאיר appears to say nothing about the first clause.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי מאיר treats 'died vs. killed' as a contradiction, then 'died vs. did not die' is surely one too. He should disagree there as well.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: רבי מאיר does disagree there
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the first clause really is a matter of dispute. רבי מאיר disagrees there too, and the unnamed ruling follows רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It is taught as a dispute, and the first clause follows רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question by saying that רבי מאיר does argue in the first clause too. The משנה just did not spell it out there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this view, the first clause is not everyone's opinion. It is the view of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, who let the wife who said 'he died' remarry. רבי מאיר would forbid her because of the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught as a dispute (not everyone agrees)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
It is taught as a dispute,
and it is the view of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: He means the first clause, which lets the wife who said he died remarry, is their opinion and not רבי מאיר's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of why רבי מאיר does not disagree in the first clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the clause to specific תנאים: the first clause is a disputed view and not unanimous.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר seems to agree with the first clause.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר disagrees there too. The first clause follows רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even רבי מאיר agrees in the first clause
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן offers a different answer. Even רבי מאיר agrees with the first clause, because in testimony that lets a woman remarry, a claim of 'he did not die' does not count as a contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: You can even say the first clause follows רבי מאיר. In this case even רבי מאיר agrees, because any claim of 'He did not die' in testimony about a woman is not considered a contradiction.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second answer that disagrees with רבי אלעזר. He says רבי מאיר has no argument with the first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר made the first clause a dispute. רבי יוחנן instead sets a rule: in testimony about a woman's husband, 'he did not die' is not treated as a contradiction. So רבי מאיר, who forbids remarriage when there is a real contradiction (died vs. killed), would still let the wife who said 'he died' remarry.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony about a woman (allowing her to remarry)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. רבי אלעזר says רבי מאיר argues in the first clause too. רבי יוחנן says even רבי מאיר agrees there, because 'he did not die' does not count as a contradiction in a woman's testimony.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying רבי מאיר dropped his rule about contradictions. He is saying that 'he did not die' does not fall under that rule here.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
You can even say it follows Rabbi Meir,
in this case even Rabbi Meir agrees
that any 'He did not die' in testimony about a woman
is not a contradiction.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer that disagrees with רבי אלעזר's answer to the same question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a distinction: 'he did not die' is not a contradiction in a woman's testimony, so רבי מאיר's rule does not apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause must go against רבי מאיר, since he forbids remarriage when reports conflict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי מאיר agrees with the first clause, because 'he did not die' does not count as a contradiction here.

steps.title: A line in the משנה seems to contradict רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of one witness saying 'he died' against one saying 'he did not die,' where she may not marry. That fits רבי אלעזר but seems to contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if one witness says 'he died' and one says 'he did not die,' or one woman says 'he died' and one says 'he did not die,' she may not marry. This works well for רבי אלעזר, since the unnamed ruling follows רבי מאיר. But for רבי יוחנן it is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's answer from Step 6 by quoting another line of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that 'he did not die' does not count as a contradiction when it comes to letting a woman remarry. Yet here the משנה says a 'did not die' witness stops her from marrying. רבי אלעזר has no problem, because he holds this unnamed ruling follows רבי מאיר, who treats conflicting reports as blocking remarriage.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnamed ruling in the משנה

phrases.english: We learned: one witness says "he died,"
and one witness says "he did not die,"
or one woman says "he died"
and another woman says "he did not die"
she may not marry.
Granted, according to רבי אלעזר,
the unnamed ruling follows רבי מאיר,
but according to רבי יוחנן, it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר סְתָמָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 6, using a line of the משנה that fits רבי אלעזר's answer in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that 'he did not die' does not count as a contradiction for permitting remarriage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly forbids remarriage when one witness says 'did not die.' So 'did not die' does count as a contradiction, unless the unnamed ruling follows רבי מאיר, which is רבי אלעזר's view.

steps.title: The גמרא admits the difficulty stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concedes: yes, it is a difficulty for רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has no answer and simply agrees that רבי יוחנן's view faces a difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No defense is offered for רבי יוחנן, so the question stays open. The word קשיא marks an unanswered problem. It is softer than תיובתא, which would mean the view is fully knocked down.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult (the question remains unanswered)

steps.confusionAlert: קשיא here does not mean רבי יוחנן is rejected outright. That stronger word would be תיובתא. It only means the גמרא has no answer for now.
steps.whatToRemember: The question of why רבי מאיר does not argue on the first clause ends with two answers. רבי אלעזר's answer fits the משנה smoothly. רבי יוחנן's answer is left with an unresolved difficulty.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to Step 7 by conceding the difficulty.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's explanation remains with an unresolved difficulty from the משנה.

steps.title: New משנה: the wife may marry, but her rival may still eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A wife returning from overseas who says her husband died may marry and collect her כתובה. Her rival wife may not marry. According to רבי טרפון, if the rival is married to a כהן she may keep eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman went overseas with her husband, came back, and said 'my husband died.' She may marry and collect her כתובה, but her rival wife is forbidden to marry. If the rival was an Israelite woman married to a כהן, she may eat תרומה. These are the words of רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on what one wife's testimony does for herself and for her rival wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her own word is enough to free her, but she cannot testify for her צרה, so the rival stays married. רבי טרפון follows this through. Since the husband is still treated as alive for the rival, she keeps her right to eat תרומה as a כהן's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Her rival wife (another wife of the same husband)
The holy portion of produce that a כהן's household may eat
A non-כהן woman married to a כהן

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A woman who went, she and her husband,
overseas,
and she came back and said "my husband died"
she may marry and collect her כתובה,
but her rival wife is forbidden.
If she was an Israelite woman married to a כהן,
phrases.notes: "She" here means the rival wife, not the woman who testified.

phrases.english: she may eat תרומה,
these are the words of רבי טרפון.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלְכָה הִיא וּבַעְלָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The testifying wife may remarry. The rival may not. According to רבי טרפון, the rival keeps eating תרומה because her husband is still treated as alive.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the rival is strict both ways
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects רבי טרפון's leniency. The rival must be forbidden both to marry and to eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: this is not the way to keep her away from sin. She must be forbidden to marry and also forbidden to eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי טרפון about the rival wife eating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the testimony is true and the husband really died. If so, the rival might be eating תרומה when she no longer may. To stay safe from sin either way, רבי עקיבא is strict on both counts: no marrying and no תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Out of the reach of sin

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says:
This is not the way
that takes one out of the reach of sin,
phrases.notes: Literally "takes him out of the hands of sin." He means this ruling still leaves room for sinning.

phrases.english: unless she is forbidden to marry
and forbidden to eat תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין זוֹ דֶּרֶךְ מוֹצִיאָתוֹ מִידֵי עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי טרפון's ruling in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rival is forbidden both to remarry and to eat תרומה.

steps.title: Same case with the father-in-law: the mother-in-law may still eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A woman says her husband died and then her father-in-law died. She may marry and collect her כתובה. Her mother-in-law may not marry, but according to רבי טרפון she may eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said: 'My husband died, and afterward my father-in-law died.' She may marry and collect her כתובה, but her mother-in-law is forbidden to marry. If the mother-in-law was an Israelite woman married to a כהן, she may eat תרומה. These are the words of רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the same pattern with the mother-in-law in place of the rival wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A daughter-in-law cannot testify for her mother-in-law, so the mother-in-law stays married. רבי טרפון again lets her keep eating תרומה, since her husband is still treated as alive.

phrases.english: She said: "My husband died,
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets, לי, appears in some versions and not in others. It doesn't change the meaning.

phrases.english: and afterward my father-in-law died"
she may marry and collect her כתובה,
but her mother-in-law is forbidden.
If she was an Israelite woman married to a כהן,
she may eat תרומה,
these are the words of רבי טרפון.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה: מֵת לִי בַּעְלִי, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת חָמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ruling of Step 9 to the mother-in-law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The testifying woman may remarry. Her mother-in-law may not. According to רבי טרפון, the mother-in-law keeps eating תרומה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא again: the mother-in-law is strict both ways
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא repeats his view. The mother-in-law is forbidden both to marry and to eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: this is not the way to keep her away from sin. She must be forbidden to marry and also forbidden to eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the same strict ruling for the mother-in-law that he gave for the rival wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is the same as Step 10. Maybe the father-in-law really died, so eating תרומה might be a sin. To be safe either way, she is forbidden both to marry and to eat תרומה.
steps.whatToRemember: In both cases, the rival wife and the mother-in-law, the testifying woman frees only herself. רבי טרפון lets the other woman keep eating תרומה. רבי עקיבא is strict both ways.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין זוֹ דֶּרֶךְ
phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says: This is not the way
that takes her out of the reach of sin,
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, making it read 'her' (the mother-in-law).

phrases.english: unless she is forbidden to marry
and forbidden to eat תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין זוֹ דֶּרֶךְ מוֹצִיאָתָהּ מִידֵי עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי טרפון's ruling in Step 11, repeating the view from Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mother-in-law is forbidden both to remarry and to eat תרומה.

steps.title: Why the mother-in-law case was needed
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only the צרה case, we might think רבי טרפון is lenient only there, because a rival wife's jealousy is so personal. With a חמות, he might agree with רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Both cases had to be taught. If only the first case (the rival wife) had been taught, we would think רבי טרפון spoke only there, because the pain is physical. But with a mother-in-law, where the pain is only about everyday matters, we might think he agrees with רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining why the משנה repeated the same argument in two cases. This is the first half of the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rival wife shares the husband, so the jealousy is deep and personal. That makes it easy to say the wife's words cannot be trusted against her. Fights with a mother-in-law are milder, so we might think רבי טרפון would not distrust the wife there. That is why the חמות case had to be taught too.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (both cases had to be stated)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי טרפון actually agrees with רבי עקיבא about the חמות. This is only what we 'might have thought' if the משנה had given just one case.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And it is necessary
For if only that first case had been stated
I would say it is in this case that Rabbi Tarfon spoke
because the pain is physical
But a mother-in-law,
where the pain is about everyday matters
I might say he agrees with Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the משנה gave both the צרה case (Steps 9-10) and the חמות case (Steps 11-12).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The צרה case alone would suggest רבי טרפון is lenient only where the jealousy is physical, so the חמות case was needed.

steps.title: Why the rival wife case was needed
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only the חמות case, we might think רבי עקיבא is strict only there and agrees with רבי טרפון about a צרה. So both cases are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if only this case (the mother-in-law) had been taught, we would think רבי עקיבא spoke only there. But in the other case (the rival wife), we might think he agrees with רבי טרפון. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its explanation from the other side and concludes that both cases are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a חמות the wife's grudge is weaker, so being strict makes sense: she might be telling the truth. With a צרה the jealousy is so strong that we might think even רבי עקיבא would ignore her words. Teaching the צרה case shows that רבי עקיבא is strict even there.

keyTerms.meaning: That one / this one (pointing to the two cases)

steps.whatToRemember: Each case shows the strength of a different opinion. The חמות case shows רבי טרפון is lenient even with a weaker grudge. The צרה case shows רבי עקיבא is strict even with the strongest grudge.

phrases.english: And if it had been stated only in this case
phrases.notes: "This case" now means the mother-in-law case.

phrases.english: I would say it is in this case that Rabbi Akiva spoke
but in that case (the rival wife)
I might say he agrees with Rabbi Tarfon.
So it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided צריכא begun in Step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both cases are needed, because each one shows how far one of the opinions goes.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, rules like רבי טרפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling in the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון holds that a woman's words about someone she resents are simply ignored for that person. So the צרה or חמות may keep eating תרומה. We do not even worry about her words to be strict.

keyTerms.meaning: The priestly portion, which only a כהן and his household may eat

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling: testimony from someone with a grudge against the person it affects is not taken into account at all.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Tarfon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining both cases, the גמרא rules between the two opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is like רבי טרפון.

steps.title: אביי quotes a משנה about a son who died
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a later משנה. A woman claims she had a son overseas. She is believed when her claim leads to יבום, but not when it frees her from יבום. Still, the court worries about her words, so she does חליצה and not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We also learned this in a משנה. If she says, 'A son was born to me overseas. My son died and then my husband,' she is believed. If she says, 'My husband died and then my son,' she is not believed. But we take her words into account, so she does חליצה and not יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is quoting a משנה that he will use as proof for שמואל's ruling. This step sets up the proof, and the next step draws it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the son died first, the husband died with no children, so she needs יבום. She is believed about that. If the husband died first, the son was alive at the time, so she would be free of יבום. She is not believed about that, but the court still worries she may be right. That is why she does חליצה instead of יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this (in a משנה)
We take her words into account (to be strict)
She does חליצה and does not do יבום

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Abaye said: We too learned this:
phrases.notes: He is quoting a משנה found later, on 118b.

phrases.english: "A son was born to me overseas.
My son died, and afterward my husband"
she is believed.
"My husband, and afterward my son"
she is not believed.
But we are concerned about her words,
and she does chalitza and not yibum.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support שמואל's ruling in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that the הלכה is like רבי טרפון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 118b about a woman claiming her son died before or after her husband

steps.title: Only her own words count, not a rival wife's
steps.stepSummary: From the word 'her words,' אביי infers that we worry only about the woman's own claim. We do not worry about what a צרה says about her. This matches רבי טרפון, and the גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is her own words that we are concerned about. But the words of a rival wife, we are not concerned about. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws the proof from the exact wording of the משנה, and the גמרא accepts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'we are concerned about HER words.' That implies that if a צרה made the same claim about her, we would not worry at all, not even to be strict. That is exactly רבי טרפון's view: a rival's statement is ignored for the woman she resents.

keyTerms.meaning: But (this implies that...) - introduces an inference
Rival wife (another wife of the same husband)
Learn from it (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי טרפון. We do not worry at all about a rival wife's statement concerning the other woman, not even to be strict, and the משנה on 118b supports this.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the two women. In the משנה the woman's OWN words are taken into account to be strict. Only a RIVAL's words about her are ignored completely.

phrases.english: It is her own words that we are concerned about,
implying that for the words of a rival wife
we are not concerned.
Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִדְבָרֶיהָ הוּא דְּחוֹשְׁשִׁין, הָא לְדִבְרֵי צָרָה אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in Step 16.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word לִדְבָרֶיהָ ('her words') in the משנה, implying a rival wife's words are ignored
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof is accepted: a rival wife's statement is not taken into account at all, as רבי טרפון holds.
